sources.title: MiniMax-M3 official model card
sources.evidence: Exact M3 card publishes approximately 428B total and 23B activated parameters, native text/image/video processing, MSA, coding/agent capabilities, and configurable reasoning.

sources.title: MiniMax M3 launch announcement, June 1, 2026
sources.evidence: Explicitly announces the public release on June 1, 2026 with immediate API access, native image/video understanding, million-token context, MSA, and coding/agent tasks.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3 official checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration: 60 text layers, hidden size 6144, 3 initial dense/full-attention layers then 57 MoE/MSA layers, 128 routed experts/top-4 plus one shared expert, 1048576 positions. Separate 32-layer vision encoder and projection configuration; MTP fields exist.

sources.title: MiniMax Community License for M3 weights
sources.evidence: Names the MiniMax Community License. Commercial use requires attribution and notice; over US$20 million annual product/service revenue requires prior authorization. Includes prohibited-use conditions; this is not MIT or Apache-2.0.

sources.title: MiniMax OpenAI-compatible API reference
sources.evidence: The exact MiniMax-M3 row supports optional thinking; the shared M3/M3.1 parameter table includes function tools. Notes explicitly support image/video inputs for M3, with no audio input; response content is text.

sources.title: MiniMax model invocation and supported models
sources.evidence: Current supported-model table gives MiniMax-M3 a 1,000,000-token API context and says it remains available. This documents the interface; no endpoint was invoked.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3 checkpoint index and all 59 indexed safetensors headers
sources.evidence: All 23,416 indexed tensor names matched headers retrieved using bounded HTTP 206 ranges at this revision. Total stored elements: 427,040,140,160 (BF16/F32); language state 426,174,572,928; vision 631,185,920; multimodal projector 45,625,344; patch merge 188,755,968. No FP8 scales, packed tensors, or MTP tensors. The index total_size disagrees with actual headers and was not converted to parameters.

sources.title: Hugging Face MiniMax-M3 repository metadata
sources.evidence: Current revision d95e30cb912fe3021bb9c2ba66a8ce60b6c937a9. Hosted safetensors metadata reports 427,040,140,160 elements, matching the independently read headers. The repository is public and contains 59 weight shards.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3 initial Hugging Face weight commit
sources.evidence: June 12, 2026 initial commit contains the weights, config and license. This later weight upload does not replace the June 1 public/API release date.

sources.title: Later M3.1-Flash card: explicit comparison with M3
sources.evidence: Says M3.1 retains M3 core MoE architecture, replacing M3 first three full-attention layers with sparse attention and replacing the earlier EAGLE-like MTP approach with DSpark. Its own parameter specification is not transferred to M3.

sources.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention technical report
sources.evidence: Explains GQA-based block-sparse attention with learned index branches and explicitly links the production M3. Its 109B experimental model is distinct and is not used as an M3 parameter count.

sources.title: MiniMax/Hugging Face M3 reference implementation
sources.publisher: MiniMax AI Team / Hugging Face Team
sources.evidence: Defines Transformer attention/MLPs, expert routing, vision encoder and projectors. Router correction biases are registered as buffers; the checkpoint has 57 x 128 = 7,296 such elements. A raw tensor-element sum is therefore not silently asserted as an exact learned-parameter total.

sources.title: Frozen baseline Models.dev source pointer
sources.evidence: Catalog discovery pointer retained for provenance; not used to verify factual fields.

name.note: Exact official repository and API model name.

developer.note: Official MiniMax release and MiniMaxAI repository.

family.note: Retains the catalog broad MiniMax family key; the exact model is the M3 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public release/API date. Initial public weight commit is June 12; repository creation metadata is not a release event.

open_weights.note: Official public weights were directly accessible through all indexed shard headers.

license.note: Custom license with commercial attribution/notice and large-revenue authorization conditions; not an unrestricted permissive license.

parameters_b.note: Developer nominal total for M3, not an exact checkpoint count. Complete released multimodal state is 427.040140160B stored elements, including 0.865567232B vision/projectors and 7,296 routing-bias buffer elements. The BF16 checkpoint has no MTP tensors despite config fields; no missing MTP count is invented.

active_parameters_b.note: Developer nominal activated count. Its embedding/vision/MTP accounting convention is not separately defined; do not interpret it as an exact complete multimodal per-token count or replace it with the 22B reported by NVIDIA.

architecture.note: Multimodal Transformer: 60-layer text decoder with 3 dense/full-attention layers and 57 MoE/MSA layers, 128 routed experts/top-4 plus one shared expert, and a 32-layer vision encoder. MSA is sparse softmax attention, not the M1 Lightning Attention architecture.

context_window.note: Verified checkpoint max_position_embeddings. The current first-party API table separately documents 1,000,000 tokens. Preserve checkpoint capacity without claiming the API accepts 1,048,576.

modalities.note: Exact M3 API supports text, images and video and returns generated text; audio is explicitly unsupported.

reasoning.note: Official M3 card and exact API row support reasoning that can be enabled/adaptive or disabled.

tool_call.note: M3 is explicitly included in the API parameter table supporting function tool definitions.

description.value: Native multimodal MoE model using MiniMax Sparse Attention for long-context coding, reasoning, and tool use.
description.note: Describes supported architecture and documented capabilities without benchmark-superiority claims.

patch.description: Native multimodal MoE model using MiniMax Sparse Attention for long-context coding, reasoning, and tool use.
patch.notes: 428B total and 23B active are MiniMax nominal figures; active-count component accounting is not specified. All 59 BF16 shard headers total 427.040140160B stored elements, including vision/projectors and 7,296 routing-bias buffers; no MTP tensors are released in this checkpoint despite MTP config fields. Checkpoint capacity is 1,048,576 positions; the current API documents 1,000,000 tokens. Public release was June 1, 2026; the initial weight commit was June 12. Weights use the custom MiniMax Community License.

summary: Verified all 14 fields. Adds custom license, nominal 428B/23B parameters and MoE architecture; confirms June 1 release and multimodal/tool/reasoning support. Full bounded-header audit separates checkpoint state from nominal counts, confirms vision/projector coverage and absence of MTP tensors, and records API versus checkpoint context limits.
